claude_code.verification_method:
changelog + live-CLI method (automated nightly review). This cycle's automation environment DID have a live `claude` CLI (2.1.270), so `validated_against` advances on real evidence: `claude plugin validate .` passed (`√ Validation passed`) and `bash scripts/doctor.sh .` reported `healthy, with 4 optional feature(s) unavailable` (gh, shellcheck, GitHub automation, notifications — all pre-existing, environment-dependent optional gaps, not regressions). `reviewed_through`/`latest_known` advance to `2.1.270` on the official changelog. This cycle covers 2.1.269 and 2.1.270 (2026-09-11, 2026-09-12), on top of the 2.1.259–2.1.268 review already recorded below.

2.1.269 — directly relevant items: `claude plugin eval` (run a plugin's eval suite and get scored, reproducible results) is highly relevant given this plugin's 27 skills, but wiring it is a genuine design decision rather than a contained change — its case.yaml/prompt.md+graders format is unrelated to this repo's existing per-skill `evals/evals.json`/`trigger-evals.json` (skill-creator's own trigger-accuracy harness), so no suite was authored this cycle; tracked as a Future opportunity rather than adopted blind. Two hooks/permissions fixes land squarely on this repo's write-guarding hooks: a `PreToolUse` deny rule and the write-path check behind `Edit()` now also apply to a file a Bash `tee` command writes, and a `Bash(tee:*)` allow rule is now correctly scoped — this closes, at the host layer, exactly the gap `hooks/guard-sensitive-files.sh`'s own header comment documents and was built to cover independently via `hooks/lib/write-targets.py`'s `tee` parsing; `platforms/claude/settings.d/permissions-allow.json`/`permissions-ask.json` declare no `Bash(tee:*)` rule of either kind, so neither bug was ever exposed here, but the host now agrees with what this repo's own hook already enforced. A deny/ask rule starting with a bare `!` leaking beyond its settings source is fixed (a lone `!` is now ignored) — reviewed against every rule in both permission files; none starts with `!`. The attribution-reminder text overriding a project's `CLAUDE.md`/memory instruction against an appended trailer is fixed — this repo's own `CLAUDE.md` asks *for* the `Co-Authored-By` trailer (see its Commit trailer section), so the two were never in conflict, and this repo's instruction was never at risk of being silently overridden either way. SECURITY: plugin archives extracted for a session are no longer readable by other local users, no longer leave world-writable bits, and no longer leave stale files behind a re-extraction — host-side hardening with nothing to change in this repo's manifest. `/output-style [name]` now lists/switches output styles including over Remote Control and in cloud/headless sessions — an interactive/UX convenience with nothing for a plugin manifest to adopt. `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS` governs the built-in Workflow tool's concurrent-agent fan-out; this repo ships its own orchestrate-dev/worker-dev fan-out mechanism, not a Workflow-tool script, so nothing here uses it. Reviewed and found not applicable: plugin LSP servers now sending `exit` regardless of a rejected `shutdown` (no LSP server shipped here); organization plugins via managed settings not loading in headless sessions (this plugin distributes via a marketplace add + install, not managed-settings org distribution); synced plugin MCP servers not connecting on remote-session resume (the one declared server, `github`, is this plugin's own stdio server, not a synced one); `/ultrareview --post` posting a PR comment directly (no `ultrareview` skill shipped here); cloud-session skills syncing as `anthropic-skills:<name>` (no doc here names a bare skill id that this would shadow); Artifact-DB scratchpad reads no longer needing working-folder approval (no shipped skill publishes or reads an Artifact database).

2.1.270 (2026-09-12, bug-fix-only, a regression in 2.1.269): read-only git commands in Bash no longer unexpectedly ask for permission after a session has been running for a while — relevant given `permissions-allow.json` deliberately pre-allows a set of git commands to avoid exactly this kind of friction; nothing to change in this repo's manifest, just a compatibility bump.

This cycle (2026-09-15) advances through 2.1.271 and 2.1.272, on a live `claude` CLI again (installed build reports 2.1.273, newer than this review's 2.1.272 target — the changelog data available this cycle covers only through 2.1.272, so the documented baseline stops there rather than guessing at an unreviewed release; `claude plugin validate .` passed and `bash scripts/doctor.sh .` reported the same 4 pre-existing environment-dependent optional gaps as prior cycles). 2.1.272 (2026-09-15) is bug-fixes-and-reliability-only, no adoptable item. 2.1.271 (2026-09-14) — reviewed against this repo's own artifacts, not adopted blind: `omitClaudeMd` (new agent frontmatter field, lets a subagent run without user/project/local CLAUDE.md) was checked against all ten `agents/*.md` and deliberately left unset — each already loads its own canonical contract from `core/roles/*.md` explicitly, but still needs the *target* project's own CLAUDE.md for the domain conventions a reviewer or implementer judges against, so omitting it would remove needed context. Per-command `allowed_domains` for Bash/PowerShell/Monitor in auto mode with sandboxing was reviewed against `platforms/claude/settings.d/`: no PowerShell rules, no network-scoped Bash rules beyond `gh`/`git`'s own auth, and no doc here recommends running under auto mode with sandboxing, so nothing to declare. `claude plugin install`/`update --accept-command <sha256>` was reviewed against `scripts/update.sh`/`scripts/uninstall.sh`'s existing `--json` calls: neither passes `-y` or hits an interactive confirmation today, so there is no blanket-accept behavior to tighten. **Adopted (documentation, matches an existing mechanism this repo already relies on):** the Monitor watch deadline change (always at most 30 minutes, 10 in `-p` runs, replacing the no-timeout `persistent` option) — `skills/dev-workflow/pr-dev/references/ci-monitor-loop.md`'s one Monitor wrapper here already sets `timeout_ms: 1800000` and never set `persistent`, so it was already inside the new ceiling; a background command no longer starting a second copy of itself after the conversation compacts, relevant to a long `orchestrate-dev`/`worker-dev` fan-out; a stale `.git/config.lock` after a sandboxed command failure no longer breaking `git checkout -b`/`git push -u`/`git config` for the rest of the session (Linux), directly relevant since `permissions-allow.json` pre-allows `git push *`/`git remote add *`/`git init` specifically to avoid this class of friction; and cross-session `SendMessage` delivery now giving the headless sender a notice instead of holding the message silently, and no longer implying a delivered message was read — documented in `docs/user/cross-platform-workflow.md`'s Claude-Code-to-Claude-Code note, the same place the 2.1.224/2.1.225/2.1.232/2.1.247 SendMessage history already lives. Fast mode in Claude Code Remote sessions (host setting or `/fast` typed in-session) is noted in `CLAUDE.md`'s Remote and headless Claude sessions section as an interactive convenience with nothing for a manifest to adopt. No breaking changes or deprecations in the 2.1.271/2.1.272 delta. See `CLAUDE.md`'s Hooks, Subagents, Marketplace cache, and Remote and headless Claude sessions sections, `docs/user/cross-platform-workflow.md`, and `docs/engineering/build-and-release/development-workflow.md`'s Running checks section, for the full narrative including the 2.1.259–2.1.270 review this cycle builds on.

codex.verification_method: 0.146.0 was exercised on the maintainer machine; 0.147.0 through 0.152.1 support was reviewed against the official OpenAI release deltas. .codex-version tracks 0.152.1 pending the next direct CLI validation. 0.150 adds native task references and Interrupt hooks; 0.151 adds optional-MCP discovery grace, extension-side MCP result interception, and stronger per-repository plugin catalog handling; 0.152 adds package-style MCP names, per-tool output_token_limit, long app-server shell-command timeouts, and makes update_plan opt-in. 0.152.1 is a Guardian policy fix. None requires a shared plugin-manifest migration. The manifest hooks field is NOT a 0.147.0 feature: 0.147.0 is portable agent plugins (catalog install), while plugin-manifest hooks were wired into the hook runtime by openai/codex PR #19705, merged 2026-04-28, roughly twenty releases earlier. core/capabilities/platforms.json briefly recorded codex hooks as since 0.147.0 on that confusion; the exact floor has never been established here, so the registry now claims none.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which recursive (domain-nested) SKILL.md discovery was verified with `opencode debug skill`; not re-tested in this pass, so the floor is left where the evidence put it
opencode.verification_method: opencode --version on the maintainer machine (1.18.11), exercised live: opencode debug skill / debug agent / debug config against this repo and against throwaway sandboxes; agent + config field shapes cross-checked against the published JSON Schema at https://opencode.ai/config.json. latest_known from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai dist-tags.latest (1.18.29, published 2026-09-04; refreshed 2026-09-08). validated_against is deliberately not latest_known: 1.18.11 is the build actually run, and asserting 1.18.29 would be invention. MCP stays in capabilities because OpenCode reads MCP servers natively, from the 'mcp' block of opencode.json rather than .mcp.json -- but this repo ships no 'mcp' block, and docs/user/install/opencode.md tells the user to port the entries they want. That is a documented path, not a shipped artifact, so it is not the same case as the hooks gap below. core/capabilities/platforms.json validated the claim with jq -e '.mcp // {}' opencode.json, which named a key this repo has never shipped and, because the // {} fallback makes jq -e exit 0 on every input, could not have failed if it had. reviewed_through advances to 1.18.29 on a documentary review of every release from 1.18.12 to 1.18.29 (all 18 tags retrieved individually from the GitHub Releases API; none unverified), supplemented by path-scoped commit history for 2026-08-03..2026-09-05 over src/skill, src/agent, src/config and src/mcp. No breaking change, no $schema or schema-URL change, no change to skill discovery or nesting, no change to agent frontmatter, no change to how MCP servers are declared -- and for skills and MCP that rests on zero commits to the implementing trees in the window, not merely on absence from the release notes. Two things worth carrying forward: 1.18.16 made the config parser ignore unknown top-level fields at runtime although the published schema still sets additionalProperties:false, and 1.18.24 added read-compat for v2 config, whose 'skills' is a flat array rather than this repo's v1 {paths,urls} object -- a future v2 adoption is a real opencode.json shape change even though v1 stays native today. Also confirmed from the loader glob '{agent,agents}/**/*.md' that this repo's singular .opencode/agent/ is supported outright, not merely tolerated. The review is documentary, so validated_against stays at 1.18.11.

capability_gaps.hooks: OpenCode has no hooks.json; its only lifecycle mechanism is the JS/TS plugin API, and this repo ships no plugin module by design (it would add a Node runtime dependency for no other gain). As installed, the hooks/ guards do not run at all — 'adapter' would imply a generated artifact exists, as it does for subagents, and none does.
capability_gaps.plugin_marketplace: No plugin marketplace — install is by absolute skills.paths. Not by symlink: OpenCode does not follow them for skill discovery (see the skills row).

gemini_cli.supported_min_source: Gemini CLI documents no minimum for extensions; the floor is the version the adapter was actually exercised on rather than guessed
gemini_cli.verification_method: gemini --version on the maintainer machine (0.55.1); extension format, skill discovery depth, agent validation, and hook config shape measured directly with a probe extension linked into an isolated HOME. Gemini reads skills exactly one level below a skills root, so the canonical two-level skills/<domain>/<name>/ tree resolved to zero; scripts/build-gemini-extension.sh generates a flat symlink mirror at .gemini/skills/ plus translated sub-agents at .gemini/agents/, both committed and drift-checked. Verified live: 30 of 30 skills discovered, all 10 agents load with zero errors. Registry key is gemini_cli (not gemini) so this file, core/capabilities/platforms.json and platforms/gemini/adapter.yaml all name the same platform id.

capability_gaps.plugin_marketplace: Gemini installs extensions from a git URL; there is no marketplace listing to publish to.

capability_source_note: targets.<key>.capabilities and capability_gaps are DERIVED from the capability registry and must not be hand-edited. Regenerate with `bash scripts/check-platform-targets.sh . --sync-capabilities`; `scripts/check-feature-equivalence.sh` fails when they drift.
version_claims_note: `validated_against` is the version this repo was last exercised against on a live maintainer machine. `reviewed_through` is the newest upstream release whose notes have actually been read for adapter impact. They are different claims and they drift apart on purpose: reading release notes is cheap and should always be current, while a live run needs a maintainer at a machine. V1-04 fires on `reviewed_through < latest_known` -- nobody has looked at what shipped -- because that is the gap a contributor can actually close. It deliberately does not fire on a validated_against lag, which is bounded instead by `last_reviewed` and V1-05's 90-day budget. A target with no `reviewed_through` falls back to `validated_against`, so consumer repos that have not adopted the field score exactly as before.
